title: Signal Ops standup capture — 2026-06-18
content:
Date: 2026-06-18
Purpose: Weekly bridge between observability, SRE and product telemetry teams — capture standup updates, short experiments, and immediate action items related to tracing, dashboards, and cost telemetry.

Attendees: Maya Chen (notes), Ravi Patel, Elena Gonzalez, Tom Brooks, Aisha Rahman, +1 (on-call rotation)

TL;DR:
- Rolling out adaptive trace-sampling to 10% of prod traffic (OBS-3141) — initial results show 22% reduction in stored spans and ~7% cost savings for the traces storage pipeline.
- Dashboard query timeouts still causing slow UX for model-level latency panels; temporary materialized-view approach (proof-of-concept) looks promising.
- Embeddings pipeline cost spike traced to cache miss storm after recent cache key change; patch in review (PR #422). Estimated $6k/month saving once deployed.

Standup notes (brief):
- Maya C: Adaptive sampling rollout monitoring. Need to validate tail-latency correlation with sampled traces (Ravi to pair). Working on tagging logic for warm-cache / cold-cache spans so we can separate impact. Blocker: missing trace tag on a legacy service (INF-7892).
- Ravi P: Dashboard refactor POC using hourly materialized views for heavy joins. Reduced query time from 9s -> 1.2s on sample dataset. Next: validate freshness SLA for near-real-time panels.
- Elena G: Cost telemetry ingestion pipeline — investigating high-cardinality keys from embeddings metadata. Narrowed to payload-version header mismatch, producing duplicate cache keys. Hotfix in PR; testing in staging.
- Tom B (SRE): Noticed elevated 5xx during midnight batch drains; traced to tracing exporter backpressure when spans batch grows beyond 2MB. Proposed short-term: cap batch size on exporter and async flush.
- Aisha R (platform analytics): Preparing a dashboard for per-route unit economics (tokens-in, tokens-out, latency bins). Needs a join key from tracing to map request-id -> route; opened OBS-3204 to add the lightweight request_id tag to the router shim.

Open experiments and quick wins:
- Adaptive sampling: 10% rollout for low-QPS endpoints; collect p99 latency and error-rate delta. Target: <1% change in p99 across endpoints. Estimated cost saving: $7k–$10k/mo if successful.
- Materialized views for heavy dashboards: create hourly MV for model-latency panels, maintain 30min freshness window. Early tests show >6x faster queries. Risk: slightly stale view for spike debugging.
- KV-cache span tagging: add "cache_hit" boolean and "cache_tier" string to spans to separate cache vs compute latency in traces. Helps attribute cost to cache misses.

Decisions taken:
- Approve temporary exporter batch-size cap during peak midnight drains. Tom will implement and monitor for 48h.
- Proceed with materialized view POC for latency dashboards; Ravi to coordinate with infra for MV refresh orchestration.

Action items (owner — due):
- Ravi P — finish MV orchestration prototype and run load test against staging dashboards (due 2026-06-24).
- Maya C & Ravi P — pair on sampled-trace tail-latency correlation test (due 2026-06-20).
- Elena G — merge cache-key hotfix PR and run controlled deploy to staging (PR #422) (due 2026-06-19).
- Tom B — apply exporter batch-size cap on canary fleet and report metrics (due 2026-06-19).
- Aisha R — finalize per-route economics dashboard wireframe and link to OBS-3204 (due 2026-06-25).

Blockers / risks:
- Legacy service missing standardized trace headers (INF-7892) — prevents reliable correlation across router -> worker hops. Needs small SDK patch; blocked by owner's bandwidth.
- Cost telemetry ingestion churn due to high-cardinality metadata — if not addressed, ingestion costs may exceed forecast for Q3.
- Dashboard staleness tradeoff: MVs improve UX but may mask short spikes; need a clear escalation path for ad-hoc live queries.

Metrics snapshot (quick numbers from morning run):
- Traces ingested (last 24h): ~2.1M spans (down from 2.7M baseline after initial sampling tests)
- Trace storage bytes/day: ~120GB (projected 3.6TB/mo)
- Dashboard query p95 (model-latency panel): 1.2s (vs 9.0s pre-MV POC)
- Observability infra cost estimate (tokens+ingestion+storage): ~$38k/month (target for Q3: $30k)
- Embeddings pipeline cost last 24h: $1,120 (spike traced to cache issue — expected to drop to ~$450 after fix)

Notes / brainstorming fragments (raw):
- Could we emit a lightweight "trace-summary" event to metrics pipeline for every request (small proto) so dashboards can show per-route counts without hitting trace storage? Pro: cheap and immediate. Con: need to instrument many services.
- Consider two-tier retention: 7d hot span store + 90d compressed archive — model offline tooling reads archive. Archive cost much lower if we compress and drop debug fields.
- Idea: Auto-adjust sampling rate by recent error-rate or latency anomalies per route. If route shows spike, increase sampling for 15m.

Related links and refs:
- OBS-3141 (adaptive-sampling rollout) — https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/OBS-3141
- OBS-3204 (request_id tagging for dashboard joins) — https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/OBS-3204
- INF-7892 (legacy header instrumentation) — https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-7892
- Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/instrumentation/pull/422
- Ops runbook (draft): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/ops-bridge-runbook

Next meeting: 2026-06-25 09:30 PT — same bridge channel (Slack: #observability-ops-bridge).

Quick TODOs to capture after this meeting:
- Attach raw CSV of query timings to OBS-3204 (Ravi)
- Add example spans for cache_hit=true/false to the instrumentation README (Maya)
- Schedule 30m sync with SRE midnight-run owners to review exporter batching plan (Tom)
